page.layout: One column of running text, with a Greek line at the top of the column. No margin notes. Page number at the head. The word "qui" at the lower right is a catchword.

main_text.p: [illegible, ~8 letters] ὀνῶ[?], καὶ λόγῳ κεκοσμημένον. Patriarcha Ignatius fama evulgata Cæsarem Bardam nu-rum fiam incestare, sæpius cum adhortatus est, ut a simili piaculo abstineret, neque esset multis offensio, qui virtutis ac pudicitiæ deberet esse exemplum. Cæsar verbis veluti aculeis punctus odia in Patriarcham nutriebat. Cum vero tandem ad communionem properantem Patriarcha repulisset, vix ille compos animi, & iracundia ardens monitorem ad frugem, veluti iniquum, & corruptorem ab Ecclesia eiicit, tormentisque insanabilibus afflixit, cogens Patriarchatu renunciare. Namque eum dedidit Theodoro cognomento Moro, nec non Ioanni Gorgonitæ, & Nicolao Scutelopi, qui in templo Apostolorum, & Constantini Copronymi urna cruribus fractis inclusum, hyemali tempestate nudum derelinquunt. Hinc Athleta ex occultis carnes putredine, & sanguine commixtas eiiciebat. Ita dira perferens fortunatissimus hic vir, non est ad Dominum malum locutus: ideoque mittit illi Dominus Constantinum Armenium, qui esset unicum illi in malis solatium. Hic etenim vasculo vitreo vini pleno, nec non & pane quandoq; etiamfructibus[?], maleficorum conatus fallens, ad Beatum accedens, eumque urna educens paululum adversos casus consolabatur, levabatque fortunas, donec denuo custodes accederent. Cæsar interim Photium in Patriarchatum promouit,

page.notes: The first Greek line at the head is only partly legible; the opening word is illegible and "ὀνῶ" and "κεκοσμημένον" are uncertain. "quandoq;" and "etiamfructibus" are doubtful readings. "adversos" was read as "aduersos" in the scan and is written in modern u/v form. The printed word "nu-rum" is hyphenated at the line end. The bottom decoration is not printed text and is omitted.
